description: Reviewed manifest of every HTTP call made by the RADAS CLI (apps/cli) plus the classification of every command that does not call the server. Sources: Task 1.3 route-mismatch table (.superpowers/sdd/task-1.3-report.md), grep of cmd/ for c.Get/c.Post/c.Put/c.Delete/c.Do/client.Do, and the live Flask route table (app.url_map).

metadata.server_boot: scripts/export_openapi.build_contract_app (same blueprint registration as app.py, including blueprint prefixes already resolved into full url_map paths)
metadata.blueprint_prefix_accounting: Blueprint prefixes (e.g. the cloud_provisioning blueprint prefix /api/cloud) are already part of every rule string in app.url_map, so the checker compares full served paths; the manifest records full paths including prefixes.

console_current_rewriting.behavior: The console HTTP wrapper rewrites the literal path segment '/_current/' to the concrete project id (path.replace('/_current/', '/<projectId>/')) before the request leaves the browser. The server therefore never sees a literal /_current/ segment, and no server route contains it.
console_current_rewriting.manifest_policy: The CLI never uses /_current/ paths: it resolves a concrete project id (runtime config / X-Project-Id header). The checker rejects any manifest entry whose path contains a literal /_current/ segment with a dedicated diagnostic instead of comparing it against app.url_map.

metadata.path_param_syntax: Go fmt verbs (%s) in manifest paths denote a single literal path segment sent by the CLI; the checker matches them against Flask variable segments (<name>, <int:name>, ...).
metadata.known_mismatches_initial_table: The initial (pre-fix) manifest for Task 2.4 marked these as failing entries (kind remote-broken where applicable): approval list GET /api/approvals/pending (no server route), audit list GET /api/audit?action=&user= (server serves GET /api/audit-log), user invite POST /api/users/invite (server serves POST /api/users/invites), cost estimate GET /api/finops/estimate/<id> (no server route), policy exempt POST /api/policies/exemptions (no server route), org rules GET/POST /api/orgs/<id>/rules (no server route), worker drain POST /api/workers/<id>/drain (no drain route), registry publish from local dir (server publishes from server-side stacks), cloud provider probe (no ad-hoc probe endpoint), cloud inventory (needs a stack/account selector), flags get GET /api/flags/<key> (never registered; found by this checker during Task 2.4), state unlock (fake success with no server call). Each is now fixed to a real route or reclassified kind=local with an explicit decision note; tests/test_route_parity.py pins this mapping so nothing is waived silently.
